facts.fact: The column says Powertel and Paratus Zimbabwe formed an equal-investment PPP to build a DWDM fibre backhaul network across Zimbabwe delivering up to 10 Tbps of cross-border bandwidth linking Zimbabwe, Botswana and Zambia; it gives no agreement date, so the published date is used.

The column says the Powertel-Paratus network starts with an active 800 Gbps link between Plumtree and Bulawayo; it gives no date for it, so the published date is used, and it names no other country's traffic carried.

The column says TelOne has ongoing backbone capacity expansions along cross-border transit links such as Kazungula to Zambia/Botswana and Beitbridge to South Africa; no date is given, so the published date is used.

facts.fact: POTRAZ says the African Union Commission awarded it a USD 200,000 grant in 2015 under the AU Regional Internet Exchanges Initiative to set up the Harare Regional Internet Exchange Point; the grantor is the AU, no other country is named.

POTRAZ says in its 2020 forum contribution that HIX needs to attract more regional players to connect and peer to become a proper regional IXP, and that all connected members are access providers with two international peers (Packet Clearing House, Quad9); the document is undated, so the forum opening date is used.

Paratus says Powertel Communications and Paratus Zimbabwe signed a PPP agreement in June 2025 to jointly invest in high-capacity long-distance fibre in Zimbabwe, the Botswana-Zimbabwe-Zambia corridor, with an IRU between them.
Paratus says the second phase, connecting Bulawayo and Livingstone (Zambia), is due to be lit in September 2026 to complete the three-country corridor.

Paratus and Powertel announce the first phase, Plumtree to Bulawayo, is live and carrying traffic with 800 Gbps equipped capacity, as the first active Paratus-connected fibre route into Zimbabwe linking it to Botswana, Zambia and South Africa; no other country's operator or traffic figure is given.

facts.fact: NewsDay reports the first operational section, Plumtree-Bulawayo, of the Powertel-Paratus Zimbabwe fibre corridor to Botswana is live and carrying traffic at 800Gbps initial capacity.
NewsDay reports the second phase, extending the corridor from Bulawayo to Livingstone in Zambia, is under construction and expected to be commissioned in September 2026.

NewsDay reports the project runs under a public-private partnership signed in June 2025 with Paratus, plus an Indefeasible Right of Use agreement giving Paratus capacity while Powertel keeps operational control.
